articles.title: The one change that worked: I was burnt out and lonely – until I started ice skating
articles.summary: I was stressed and newly diagnosed with ADHD when I decided to choose a new hobby. It awakened my playfulness and immediately improved my quality of life. In 2024, I decided to return to England after four and a half years in Lisbon. My first winter back in the UK was psychologically challenging.
body: During this time, I was diagnosed with combined-type attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). I used to think I was depressed, but my diagnosis made me realise that part of how I felt was burnout – my brain’s ability to regulate stress was depleted. I felt overwhelmed and would shut down, which would lead to cycles of anxiety, depression and self-criticism.

I needed a new hobby, so I chose ice skating. The effect it had on my quality of life was immediate. I skated twice a week, once in a private lesson with a friend and once in a group lesson. The social connection and sense of progress added structure and joy to my sometimes shapeless weeks. Friends who had always said I was “all or nothing” joked that I would drop my new hobby when things got tough, but I persisted.

articles.title: Not ready for the cold and dark? Maybe you need a ‘winter transition week’ | Emma Beddington
articles.summary: A psychologist has recommended we all take time for slowness and rest, to prepare ourselves for the coming months. It’s a nice idea, but it may prove my downfall. How are you feeling about the rapid dying of the light?
body: Leibowitz, the author of a book, How to Winter, based on her time living in the Arctic, explains: “I intentionally clear out my calendar … say no to extra obligations, try to cancel or postpone unnecessary meetings and make time for rest and slowness.” During this time, she also recommends stocking up on tea, getting out thick socks, eating soup and planning little treats.

My issue with this good, if hardly groundbreaking, advice is: how do you transition out again? Because a regime of “rest and slowness”, refusing all engagements, sipping soup while swaddled like a baby in blankets and indulging in little treats is sensible for a week, but it will become my entire life if I let it.

articles.title: My search for Bologna’s perfect tagliatelle al ragù - the real ‘spag bol’
articles.summary: The signature dish of Italy’s gastronomic capital is taken far more seriously than its British derivative. So which restaurant does the best ‘tag rag’? I used to eat spag bol three times a week. I’d have it every Friday at my nan’s, every Saturday at my dad’s, and every Tuesday at my mum’s.
body: I’m not alone in being a big fan of spag bol – the dish is often voted the nation’s favourite, and there’s now even a National Spaghetti Bolognese Day (22 May) – but I do sometimes wonder what it is about this relatively simple import, essentially a combo of mince and tomatoes plonked upon pasta, that has won over millions and withstood the vagaries of time. So I travelled to the dish’s motherland, Bologna, to unlock its secrets and hunt down some prime examples.

No sooner had I arrived in the city, which is roughly equidistant between Venice and Florence, than it became alarmingly apparent that I didn’t have a clue what I was on about – the sauce is called ragù, for a start, and is never served with spaghetti (the use of which is often attributed to Elizabeth David, who called for it in her 1954 book Italian Food). The pasta must be tagliatelle, and by official decree an authentic tagliatella must be precisely 8 millimetres wide, so that the rough, hand-rolled egg pasta ( sfoglia ) grips the slow-cooked meat sauce perfectly.
Notwithstanding my naivety, here are five spots in Bologna where the tagliatelle al ragù alla bolognese (or tag rag for short) proved a hit with my taste buds.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Mr Baxter, who ate our belongings – and broke our hearts
articles.summary: Reared on a puppy farm, and abandoned by a previous owner, he was half-starved when we adopted him. But he grew strong, chomping through everything from dog beds to sunglasses and my debut book.
body: The day we brought our 14-week-old cocker spaniel home in 2022, I was wearing a silk scarf I’d picked up decades ago in a vintage shop in Tokyo. I didn’t know it then but that rainy afternoon would be the last time I’d wear it. Three days later, it was in my new puppy’s mouth. Once he’d finished tearing my scarf to shreds, he gazed at me with soulful chocolate brown eyes, fluttering his long eyelashes.

No matter how fond I was of that silk scarf, how could I be angry? Puppies chew stuff. That’s what they do. Mr Baxter gnawed his way through four dog beds, blankets and multiple dog leads. Nothing was off-limits. Socks, shoes, trainers, gloves, flat caps, berets, the freshly printed chapters of my debut book, a nifty pair of 70s sunglasses. Fearless and lithe, he grabbed things we naively thought were out of reach, and woe betide anyone who tried to take them from him.

But he grew strong, chomping through everything from dog beds to sunglasses and my debut book.

articles.title: Millions Will Travel for Thanksgiving as Air Traffic Recovers From Outage
articles.summary: Travelers at Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport in Atlanta on Friday, when a nationwide ground stop caused serious flight delays and cancellations.
body: Nearly six million Americans are expected to fly over the Thanksgiving holiday despite soaring ticket prices and an air traffic system that is still recovering after a nationwide ground stop stranded millions of passengers on Friday and into the weekend.

AAA, the automobile owners group that also tracks air travel, projects that 5.96 million travelers will take domestic flights between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. They are expected to spend 17 percent more than they did last year on tickets, with round-trip fares averaging $800.

The forecast is a 0.2 percent dip from a record travel rush last year, but it comes as passengers are scrambling to salvage plans after a glitch in an air traffic control upgrade on Friday forced a ground stop for nearly five hours and caused thousands of delays and cancellations.

Flight schedules were expected to normalize on Monday, with 73 of 25,586 flights departing from the United States canceled, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics firm. As of Sunday night, 88 percent of flights departed on time, which is “above average and a sign of return to normal operations,” the firm said.

articles.title: American Global Health Aid Isn’t Dead. It’s Changing.
articles.summary: Members of the pharmacology department at Lodwar County Referral Hospital in Kenya took inventory of the last boxes of drugs delivered by U.S.A.I.D. last April.
body: Americans might have assumed that their country was out of the business of promoting global health. On his first day in office, President Trump announced the United States’ withdrawal from the World Health Organization and abruptly “paused” foreign aid. Over the following weeks, Elon Musk took a chain saw to the U.S. Agency for International Development.

In the wake of these actions, reporters documented shortages of tuberculosis, malaria and H.I.V. drugs, widespread clinic closures and the abandonment of patients enrolled in medical trials. Many programs never resumed, and researchers predicted that hundreds of thousands of avoidable deaths would occur in the first year alone. Assessing whether this came true is complicated by the fact that programs tracking health outcomes were among those the U.S. ended.

articles.title: 28 Black-Tie Wedding Guest Dresses That Are Perfectly Formal
articles.summary: From sequined gowns to maximalist florals, our edit of the best black-tie wedding guest dresses will help you master the formal attire dress code.
body: The main thing to keep in mind is the definition of the dress code. Put simply, “black tie” means floor-length hemlines, so leave the midi dress at home in favor of something ankle-sweeping. From there, you’ll find there’s a lot of variation within the black-tie wedding guest dress options.

If you’re stuck on where to start, begin by considering the setting. A black-tie event in an upscale city venue requires a different sort of formal dress than a black-tie event in a bucolic setting. Think about fabrics and the season, as well as silhouette: Do you go light and dreamy, with layers of tulle and pleated chiffon? Or moody and sophisticated with luxe silk and embroidered jacquard? When in doubt, a classic A-line or halterneck style offers just enough formality. And for winter weddings, anything in rich tones, from golden saffron to oxblood to inky navy, is a safe bet.

articles.title: Research Stalls for a Year Into a Cancer That Kills Children in a Year
articles.summary: For 27 years, the Pediatric Brain Tumor Consortium worked to save kids with brain cancer. But just before 5-year-old Ryleigh Schecter was diagnosed, the government shut it down.
body: When Ryleigh Schecter answered the front door to her home, she was wearing an oversized lavender bow in her hair that matched the stripes on her shirt. “Rainbow” is her favorite color, she told me as I sat with her and her parents, Amanda and Aaron, in their cozy living room in Twinsburg, Ohio. To prove it, she recited the colors of the spectrum in order, adding “pink, silver, gold” at the end. She is 5.

Eventually, the Schecters and I began to talk about the medicine she takes, and on cue Ryleigh sped to the kitchen and raced back with a sandwich bag full of Skittles. It contained only the red, orange and yellow ones. “I don’t like the purple or the green,” she explained.
Ryleigh takes two drugs every night, one designed to treat breast cancer. Her mother mixes them as if from a chemistry set and administers them orally with a syringe. Ryleigh hates them.
“The first one tastes disgusting, and the second one tastes medium,” Ryleigh told me.

articles.title: An Inside Guide to Kate Middleton’s Royal Tour Wardrobe in India
articles.summary: Ahead of the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess of Wales have touched down in India for the first time in a decade. See every look Kate Middleton wears during the royal tour.
body: India had sat at the top of Kate Middleton ’s bucket list ever since she married into the royal family in 2011. Or so said Prince William during their 2016 tour of the subcontinent, for which the then Duchess of Cambridge packed a wardrobe that brought together the fashion heritage of both India and the country she represented.

First came an Alexander McQueen dress, its paisley print drawing on the textile traditions of India and Persia, followed by a pink-and-pistachio tunic dress by Mumbai-based designer Anita Dongre, worn to play cricket at the Oval Maidan with children supported by local charities. Then along came a Jenny Packham gown, hand-beaded by Indian artisans, to a Bollywood gala, and a blue-and-white embroidered sheath dress by Cumballa Hill-born designer Naeem Khan for a visit to the Taj Mahal. Together, the looks offered an early indication of Kate’s understanding of clothing as a diplomatic tool.

articles.title: What Are Thanksgiving Sides That Don’t Need to Go in the Oven?
articles.summary: Air fryer brussels sprouts, adult mac and cheese, steamed sweet potatoes, and more hand-picked recipes.
body: There are millions of recipes on the internet, but you still don’t know what to cook. Tell us about it! Dear Bon Appétit is an advice column where we answer your culinary conundrums with hand-picked recipes and well-seasoned advice. Submit a question here.

If there was a proverbial dartboard of Thanksgiving problems, you have just hit the bullseye. (And as someone who has never hit a real bullseye in her life, I mean this as quite the compliment!) Even if you place oven racks strategically—even if you have one of those fancy double ovens—there’s always a bottleneck of dishes that need to be roasted and baked.
The solution is not to plot out an overwrought schedule of when things go in and out, and in and out, but to ruthlessly reduce the number of recipes that require the oven in the first place.

With that in mind, I would like to point out that turkey can thrive in other settings. And no, I’m not talking about deep-frying it in your yard, which we all know is a rowdy and risky idea, as proven in Gilmore Girls season three episode nine. You could grill it. You could smoke it. Both delightful.

articles.title: Herby Sheet-Pan Meatballs With Feta
articles.summary: Oven-baked, mess-free, and topped with so much cheese.
body: These aren’t your slow-braised, leisurely Sunday-sauce meatballs. They’re let’s-get-this-crew-fed-at-the-end-of-a-busy-workday meatballs. The large amount of breadcrumbs isn’t just a filler; combined with the water, they make the meatballs impossibly tender and springy. You can use any ground meat you’d like; pork, lamb, turkey, or chicken (only dark meat for the poultry, though) all work well. Roasting the meatballs in the oven instead of frying them on the stovetop reduces the active cook time and makes cleanup simple.

Place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 425°. Using a sturdy wooden spoon, vigorously mix 2 large eggs, zest of 1 lemon, 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, 1 cup panko, ½ cup finely chopped dill and/or parsley, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 2 tsp. dried oregano, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, 1 tsp. ground cumin, and ½ cup water in a large bowl until nearly a smooth paste. Add 1 lb. ground beef and mix vigorously until well combined and mixture is slightly tacky. Oil your hands; divide mixture into 16 portions and roll into balls. Arrange on a large rimmed baking sheet.
